messages:
devin: Heads-up — we just got a customer escalation (acct: acme-markets) reporting inconsistent completions in the same conversation. They say outputs flip between concise and verbose answers mid-session. :eyes:

sara: Is this the routing/fallback noise again? Any request IDs from the customer?

devin: They included a few request_ids, e.g. req_2023112201 and req_2023112204. Both within the same convo_id. They captured responses that look like different model variants (one is long-form, one short).

raj: That sounds like model-variant handoff. Did we rollout the new quantized rdl-2-lite yesterday?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Completed rollout "rdl-2-lite-canary" to 30% routing at 2024-11-22T03:12:11Z :rocket:

emily: Customer says this started right after yesterday's rollout. They have a replay sequence in the ticket. Asking for a reproducible check.

devin: Repro steps from ticket (paraphrased):
1) Start chat (convo_id=abc123)
2) Send prompt1 -> get verbose answer (looks like rdl-2-full)
3) Send prompt2 -> get short answer (like rdl-2-lite)
4) Repeat: sometimes mixes again

sara: Can we confirm routing metadata for those req ids? If requests for same convo are hitting different model variants, routing is leaking per-request instead of per-session.

raj: Checking router logs now. Short snippet for req_2023112201:
```
2024-11-22T04:01:05Z request=req_2023112201 tenant=acme-markets convo=abc123 route=rdl-2-full node=gpu-45
2024-11-22T04:01:06Z fallback_check passed cached_kv=false
```
And for req_2023112204:
```
2024-11-22T04:01:12Z request=req_2023112204 tenant=acme-markets convo=abc123 route=rdl-2-lite node=gpu-12
```

emily: So routing decided differently. Is routing key evaluation using only request headers? Should be using convo cookie or session id.

devin: Our routing policy is supposed to pin by (tenant, convo_id) when convo_id present. If convo_id is missing or different, it can route per-request. Maybe the customer's client is rotating convo_id? But they claim same convo id.

sara: Ask customer to resend exact request headers (convo_id, x-tenant-shard, user-agent). Also request raw request bodies.

devin: I asked the support ticket for headers and replay HAR. Customer sent back two HTTP frames — convo_id same in both. They also include an x-tenant-shard header that alternates between "s-1" and "s-2" (they use multi-shard SDK).

raj: Aha. Our smart-routing has a recent change: when x-tenant-shard is present it includes it in the routing key to avoid cross-shard overcommit. That would explain interleaving if their SDK toggles shard per request. But we also had a bug where pinning logic fell back to request-level key if header set. Looks like the rollout activated that code path.

emily: So sequence: rollout introduced new routing key behavior -> for customers with varying x-tenant-shard the router mixes variants mid-session -> visible as output quality regressions.

devin: Proposed immediate actions: 1) Hotfix router to prefer convo_id pinning over shard header 2) Roll back the rollout to 0% for tiered customers until hotfix deployed 3) Provide customer with mitigation steps (pin shard in SDK or send sticky-shard header)

ml-oncall: I can validate model differences and confirm outputs were from different variants. If we rollback routing, check that caches and KV contexts map correctly — switching variants mid-convo may orphan KV caches and cause odd completions.

raj: Working on hotfix PR now. ETA ~45m. Will also run a quick replay against both variants to show diff and add to ticket.

emily: I've told customer we're investigating and suggested they temporarily set their SDK to single-shard mode. They're okay with a short rollback window.

devin: Thanks team. Keep updates here. If we need exec escalation, I'll loop in support-lead. :thumbsup:
